executive_summary: **Both blocking and the classifier limit performance at full scale, and the classifier limits it more.** On 50,000 Source-1 entities against the complete target files (10,000 identical validation entities), the unchanged Phase 2 baseline B0 reaches macro F0.5 0.8772 [0.8727, 0.8813], not the 0.9709 of the development setting: its candidate recall falls from about 98.1% on 100,000-record target pools to 91.25% on the full files, and its logistic regression misses 4,357 retrieved positives while making 1,353 false merges.

The frozen hardened configuration scores **0.9309 [0.9279, 0.9340]** at threshold 0.8, a paired improvement of +0.0537 [0.0497, 0.0577] over B0. Improved blocking alone (B0's logistic regression on the new candidate set) raises candidate recall to 95.25% and macro F0.5 by +0.0067 [0.0041, 0.0090]; replacing the model with gradient boosting on the same candidates adds the rest (+0.0471), cutting false positives from 1,427 to 916 and classifier misses from 5,350 to 2,872. Blocking still loses 1,604 validation positives, the ceiling Phase 3 inherits.

B0 was reproduced byte-for-byte before any change and again on the final code; every comparison uses identical validation entities, seed 42 and paired bootstrap confidence intervals; no improvement is credited from a lower-recall candidate set (the frozen candidate set has higher recall than B0). Test data has not been used for any choice: after the configuration was frozen, a development-scale smoke test ran test inference on a 5,000-entity test subset only to check that the frozen pipeline runs end to end and passes the validator; no labels exist for test, nothing was changed afterwards, and no Phase 2.5 result reads its output.
name_edit_sim: The negative `name_edit_sim` coefficient is a multicollinearity artifact, not a harmful feature: on its own its standardized coefficient is positive at both scales, it correlates at r ≥ 0.9 with `name_translit_edit_sim` and `name_char3_jaccard`, and removing it changes macro F0.5 by an amount indistinguishable from zero (10k: -0.0017 [-0.0042, 0.0011]). It was kept; gradient boosting is insensitive to it.
final_configuration:
Frozen in `phase2/config/phase2_5_frozen.yaml` (derived from the B0 config; every other value unchanged):

| setting | B0 | frozen | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocking rules | 8 | 8 + house_locality, state_locality, address_signature | 10k: together they retrieve 618 (S2) and 708 (S3) positives B0 missed, with buckets bounded by the 100-record cutoff; name_phonetic_token retrieves 1 and 3 and lowers recall after the cap; postal_locality retrieves 3 and 1 (postcodes are rare) |
| max_candidates_per_source1 | 60 | 100 | chosen (05:27) from the 10k full-target sweep on the B0 rules, cutoff 100: cap 100 92.40% / 92.58% vs cap 150 92.52% / 92.66% (S2 / S3); then confirmed unchanged (06:03) by a sweep on the exact frozen rule set: 94.47% / 94.32% at cap 60, 95.25% / 95.30% at cap 100, 95.36% / 95.49% at cap 150; cap 150 adds 0.1-0.2 points for about 14% more pairs |
| max_block_size (cutoff) | 100 | 100 | B0 rules at 10k: cutoffs 50-500 measured; on the frozen rule set (cutoffs 100 and 150 only) cutoff 150 at cap 100 adds 0.3 points for about 18% more pairs (95.58% / 95.54%); not worth the feature cost and memory |
| source1_chunk_size | 100000 | 25000 | memory only: candidates and features are computed per S1, so results do not depend on the chunk size; smaller chunks bound the feature buffers for the full run |
| gradient boosting max_iter | n/a | 200 | the value evaluated in Step 9; deliberately not tuned |
| model | StandardScaler + LogisticRegression | HistGradientBoostingClassifier (max_iter 200, seed 42) | 10k, B0 candidates: 0.9172 [0.9097, 0.9249] vs 0.8758, paired +0.0414 [0.0329, 0.0494]; dev: 0.9765 vs 0.9709 |
| features | 47 | 42 (F3: the five matched_by_* block-membership flags removed) | equivalent to 47 under gradient boosting at dev and 10k (paired CI of the difference contains 0), so the simpler set is preferred |
| threshold | 0.70 (dev) | 0.8 (validation, 50k) | selected on validation macro F0.5 only |

resources: Measured: 50k Source-1 entities against the full targets take 18 minutes end to end for the frozen configuration (training and validation), with a main-process peak of 8,045 MB; the 10k harness run peaked at 9,654 MB because it holds 13 rules' key tables plus experiment buffers. Target normalization (about 2 minutes per source) and index building (about 5 minutes per source) are fixed costs; candidate joins, the cap and features scale with Source-1 count. Projected full test inference (1.73M Source-1 entities): about 216 million candidate pairs and about 1.6 hours for candidates and features; model scoring of about 216 million rows, loading and normalizing the test Source-1 file, the submission merge and validation were not measured at scale and add to this (an estimate of 2 to 3 hours in total). Peak memory was measured only for training and validation (8.0 GB at 50k); the inference path was profiled only at development scale, so the full run should be monitored; the frozen config uses 25,000 Source-1 entities per chunk to bound feature buffers. The challenge validator keeps every candidate id in memory; for a candidate_pairs.tsv of about 216 million ids it must be run on Source-1 shards (each shard with its own test_source1 subset) on a 16 GB machine.
limitations: Blocking still misses 1,604 of the validation positives at 50k (candidate recall 95.25%); at 10k most B0 misses were suppressed high-frequency keys (453 of 600), and the no-cutoff diagnostic shows up to 99% of positives share some key, so the remaining recall sits in buckets too large to enumerate.
The classifier still misses 2,872 retrieved positives and makes 916 false merges on 10,000 validation entities; recall (0.8706) remains the weaker side.

The per-S1 cap ranks by the number of retrieving rules and edit similarity; adding rules can push true pairs out of the cap (observed for name_phonetic_token), so any new rule must be evaluated after the cap.
Cross-script and transliterated names are only partly recovered by deterministic romanization and the consonant skeleton; the per-token phonetic block did not help at full scale.
Validation macro F0.5 is selected and reported on the same validation entities (the Phase 2 protocol); the threshold curve is flat around the optimum, but a small optimism remains.
France appears only in the test set; it is handled by the same country-agnostic rules without training examples.
All Phase 2.5 measurements are on Source-1 samples (5k to 50k); the full-scale figures are projections until the full run is executed.
handoff: Start from `phase2/config/phase2_5_frozen.yaml` and the frozen code; reproduce `phase2/output/phase2_5/frozen_50000/` (macro F0.5 0.9309) before changing anything.

Largest remaining lever on the blocking side: selective composite keys for oversized buckets (for example a rare name token combined with a locality token) instead of skipping them, evaluated after the cap.

Largest lever on the model side: more training entities than 40,000 and features that separate near-duplicate businesses at the same address; gradient boosting hyperparameters were deliberately not tuned.
Keep the evaluation protocol: identical validation entities, seed 42, paired bootstrap, recall reported alongside every F0.5.
The full Source-1 / full target run and the test submission are pending the user's approval (runtime and memory projection in section 13).
dependencies: Allowed list plus one documented exception approved by the user: pandas, numpy, scikit-learn (LogisticRegression, HistGradientBoostingClassifier, StandardScaler), pyyaml, pytest, and — carried over from the Phase 2 specification — rapidfuzz (edit similarity, token-set ratio) and joblib (worker processes, model persistence). No other third-party package; memory was measured externally with Windows PowerShell (`phase2/tools/memwatch.ps1`). No external data, no LLM or API, raw datasets unchanged.
